thread_analysis.thread_summary: Sharp Corporation (contact Daisuke Kamata) engages Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Masaya Iida) for a new Bluetooth SIG registration triggered by a BLE module EOL replacement (switching to a Chinese NOKE-made module while keeping the same product name/model number), spanning December 2024 through February 2025. The thread covers the full registration lifecycle for a customer working with SIG's redesigned registration system for the first time, surfacing useful practical guidance on registration staggering strategy and Review Page interpretation.
all_questions_found: How can a customer preview what will be publicly visible before Submission, what does a TCW ID number mean, and are blank auto-populated Member Detail fields a problem? (see thread_0058_case_01)
Are there SIG rules limiting registration to one model at a time, and should multiple models be registered simultaneously or staggered? (see thread_0058_case_02)

(Administrative, not separately cased) Module EOL replacement requiring new registration despite unchanged product name/model number (consistent with already-documented module-change rules elsewhere in this corpus), subcontracting-law applicability and order-confirmation-via-email-or-Invoice practice, Chinese New Year holiday timing accommodation for manufacturer-sourced documentation, and standard quote/payment/Compliance-Folder-shipment administrative sequence.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Case_01 provides valuable, previously undocumented clarity on three distinct points of confusion that arise specifically from SIG's redesigned registration system (QPRDv3.0): the lack of a formal public-visibility preview before Submission, the precise SIG-side-fault scope of TCW references, and the harmlessness of blank auto-populated Member Detail fields. Case_02's staggered-registration recommendation is a useful, reusable practical strategy for any customer managing a multi-model product family.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0058_case_01 and thread_0058_case_02 for case-specific decision logic.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_01's TCW misunderstanding risk and case_02's entry-error risk are both relatively low-stakes but easily avoidable with proactive guidance.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified -- the consultant patiently worked through a first-time user's confusion with the redesigned registration system, providing concrete workarounds (comparable-registration lookup) and precise terminology clarification (TCW's SIG-side-fault scope) rather than generic reassurance.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer is working with SIG's redesigned registration system for the first time, proactively anticipate and address common points of confusion (public-visibility preview, TCW meaning, blank Member Detail fields) before they become support tickets, and recommend staggered single-model registration over batched multi-model submission to minimize entry-error risk given the lack of a direct Product List edit function.
